title: Prospective cohort study 'Risk birth cohort Oldenburg (RisikO)' - perinatal course
summary:
High-risk births are pregnancies that pose an increased risk to the health of the child and/or parents around the time of birth. A significant form of high-risk birth is premature birth (<37+0 weeks of pregnancy), which accounts for >60,000 births per year in Germany. It is unclear why some children show acute or chronic health impairments after a high-risk birth, while other children develop normally.

The “RisikO” study integrates important findings from other cohort studies to investigate how risks can be identified, better understood, and specifically reduced during the perinatal and early postnatal periods. In particular, the aim is to better understand the complex interaction of child and parental factors and to analyze them in an interdisciplinary manner. Diagnostic, preventive, and therapeutic strategies will be identified using risk markers in order to improve care for high-risk births.

interventions.name: Premature infants with a gestational age of 23+0 to 36+6 weeks of pregnancy and full-term infants with a gestational age of 37+0 to 40+0 weeks of pregnancy with pregnancy- or birth-related risk factors will be prospectively included in the study. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Premature babies with a gestational age of 23+0 to 36+6 weeks of pregnancy and full-term newborns with a gestational age of 37+0 to 40+0 weeks of pregnancy with pregnancyor birth-related risk factors who are born at the Perinatal Center at Oldenburg Hospital AöR and whose parents consent to the scientific research.
Exclusion criteria:
Prenatal or postnatal diagnosed severe congenital anomalies with cardiopulmonary dysfunction that are incompatible with mid-term survival. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia or reliable trisomy 13 and 18. Metabolic defects, that lead to severe compromise for the organism. Palliativ treatment decided in the first 10 minutes of life postpartum, later change of therapeutic objective hereof excepted.
